subject: Phased ramp and billing smoothing for Q4 launch
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits

Hi Sean,

We're lining up a concentrated marketing + partner push for our new product in mid-October and evaluating vendor spend for inference. High level: we expect a sharp burst in the launch month (estimated 75M tokens) and a sustained but lower volume after that (20–30M tokens/mo).

Questions:
- Do you support a front-loaded/monthly step-up commit (smaller initial commit, bigger in month 2/3) with a true-up?
- Can Redwood offer a short-term launch credit (one-time accelerator) to offset initial spikes while we validate conversion?
- What would the discount slope look like across commit tiers for hosted per-token pricing?

Attached is a provisional usage forecast. Can we get a sketch of a proposal this week? We have procurement review on July 25.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director, Partnerships
BrightByte Labs
attachments: usage-forecast.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-19T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits

Emma — thanks for the clear forecast. Short answer: yes to a step-up monthly commit with a true-up, and yes we can offer a launch accelerator credit. Below is a concise proposal to start the conversation; I attached a one-page SOW sketch.

Proposal (sketch):
- Month 0 (launch month): 50M committed tokens at Tier B pricing, plus a one-time launch credit equal to 20% of Month 0 committed spend (applied to first invoice).
- Month 1: Step up to 75M committed tokens.
- Month 2+: Stabilize at 30M committed tokens with monthly true-up to actuals; over-usage billed at pay-as-you-go per-token rate or drawn from committed overage pool depending on preference.
- Discounts: Tiered per-token discounts scale by total monthly commit: Tier A (0–25M): base price; Tier B (25–75M): 12% off base; Tier C (75M+): 18% off base. We can compress thresholds for your use case.
- True-up: monthly reconciliation with ability to apply unused committed capacity forward for 2 months during launch window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will prepare a formal commercial term sheet with explicit pricing and credit mechanics.
2) If acceptable, Neha will confirm invoicing cadence / PO workflow and any seasonality protections we need in contract language.
3) We send a DocuSign-ready SOW for signature.

Looping Marissa in — Marissa, can you draft a term sheet tuned to BrightByte's forecast and include a short option for a lower upfront commit and a slightly higher launch credit?

—Sean
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: SOW-redwood-draft.pdf

On Sat, Jul 19, 2025 at 09:14 AM Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com> wrote:
> (see above)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits

Emma — good to meet you (virtually). I drafted two commercial options for your procurement team: Option 1 (lower upfront) and Option 2 (standard step-up). Key bullets below — I'll attach the term sheet PDF in the formal reply.

Option 1 — Conservative upfront:
- Month 0: 25M commit (smaller risk), launch credit = 30% of Month 0 committed spend.
- Month 1: step to 60M commit.
- Month 2+: 30M baseline.
- True-up: monthly with 60-day lookback; unused commit can be banked for up to 1 month.
- Discounting: slightly compressed: Tier B = 10% off, Tier C = 15% off.

Option 2 — Standard ramp:
- Month 0: 50M commit, launch credit = 20%.
- Month 1: 80M commit.
- Month 2+: 35M baseline.
- True-up: monthly with 2-month bank forward during launch quarter.
- Discounting: Tier B = 12%, Tier C = 18%.

Questions for procurement:
- Do you need invoicing monthly or net-30 on quarterly invoices?
- Any legal redlines on carry-forward of unused commit?

I'll slot a short term-sheet PDF to you by EOD and cc Neha for the billing/PO items.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: term-sheet-brightbyte-option1.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-21T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits — invoicing and true-up mechanics

Hi Emma — Neha on finance here. A few operational clarifications so procurement can sign off smoothly: 

1) Invoicing cadence: we can do monthly invoices with net-30, or a single monthly draw against committed balance. For launch simplicity, many customers prefer monthly invoice + credit applied to the first invoice as Sean suggested.

2) True-up mechanics: monthly reconciliation of actuals vs committed. Over-usage is invoiced monthly at pay-as-you-go, unless you elect to consume from the committed overage pool (we can set a buffer). Unused committed tokens can be carried forward for up to 60 days during the launch quarter.

3) PO / Billing contact: please provide a PO referencing deal BRB-2025-09. We can accept standard procurement PO numbers and add a short clause for seasonality (one-time launch credit and a 60-day bank-forward period).

4) Compliance asks: BrightByte will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a brief note on data retention. Sean or Karthik can route the security artifact link.

Happy to have a quick call if you want to walk the sequence — I cc'd Karthik for any technical/ops notes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma@brightbyte.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Wong <alan@brightbyte.com>
Date: 2025-07-22T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits — invoicing and true-up mechanics

Thanks Marissa / Neha — helpful. Procurement prefers lower upfront exposure, so we want Option 1 but with a slightly higher launch credit if possible. Couple of asks: 

- Can Redwood move the launch credit to 35% for Month 0 if we commit to Month 1 = 60M? That balances our risk and incentives.
- We need an example invoice schedule (sample invoice showing credit applied + month-by-month expected charges) to present at our July 25 procurement meeting.
- Do you have a DocuSign-ready SOW? Procurement will sign electronically.

Also, we will send a PO draft by EOD tomorrow. Attaching a short procurement checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emma
attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing for Q4 product push / ramp commits — finalizing next steps

Emma — we can do Option 1 with the adjusted launch credit: 35% for Month 0 if you lock Month 1 at 60M commit (BRB-2025-09). Outline of agreed commercial points below for your procurement signoff and for the DocuSign SOW we will send this afternoon.

Agreed commercial summary: 
- Month 0 (launch): 25M commit; launch accelerator credit = 35% of committed spend (applied to invoice 1).
- Month 1: 60M commit guaranteed.
- Month 2+: 30M baseline with monthly true-up and 60-day bank-forward for unused commit during the launch quarter.
- Discount tiers for this deal: Tier B (25–60M) = 10% off base; Tier C (60M+) = 15% off base for committed volume. Over-usage billed at pay-as-you-go base rate.
- Billing: monthly invoice, net-30. PO referencing BRB-2025-09 required.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II report and data-retention artifact link provided (see HubSpot link).

Action items: 
- Marissa: will send DocuSign SOW and a sample invoice showing the 35% credit applied.
- BrightByte: please send PO referencing BRB-2025-09 and countersign SOW.
- Karthik: will coordinate onboarding timeline and a short technical kickoff (we'll reserve capacity in our October launch pool).

I've created a HubSpot opportunity and linked the SOW and forecast: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/BRB-2334 (HubSpot record).

Thanks — looking forward to getting you on the platform for launch.

—Sean
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
